tagline: From the top of the East down to the Burnsville square.
intro: The drive starts where NC 128 runs out, at the parking lot just below the summit of Mount Mitchell, and goes down. NC 128 climbs over 6,400 feet, the highest road east of the Mississippi, and its only way in or out is the Blue Ridge Parkway. The drive follows the Parkway past the Black Mountains, leaves it near the twin tunnels and drops several thousand feet on NC 80 into the South Toe valley.
The South Toe runs north beside the road under the eastern face of the Black Mountains. At Micaville, named for the mica mined there, the drive turns west to Burnsville and on to Mars Hill and I-26.

moments.title: Mount Mitchell
moments.text: Elisha Mitchell measured these Black Mountains higher than New Hampshire's Mount Washington, and in 1857 he fell to his death at a nearby waterfall after coming back to check his figures.

moments.title: Micaville
moments.text: The Yancey Railroad hauled mica and feldspar out of here until storms and floods wrecked the line, and its engine number 40 was left behind by the road along 19E.

moments.title: Burnsville
moments.text: In the square Otway Burns, naval hero of the War of 1812, stands over the line "He Guarded Well Our Seas, Let Our Mountains Honor Him."

practical: If the Blue Ridge Parkway is closed for weather, NC 128 to the summit is cut off. Tractor-trailers are prohibited, and the route is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.
